detail: The help page calls it a subset of the airbnb data (869 of the 1561 Chicago listings, the same columns); Bayes Rules! fits its models on airbnb (Sections 18.2 and 19.1).

One species' late-December Ontario counts (Bald Eagle, 1981-2017), one row per year; the help page points to bird_counts as the more complete table it comes from. Bayes Rules! Exercises 12.5-12.9 model count by year and hours without grouping.
One row per movie with its release year and Bechdel result; year classifies the movies, and no model groups them. Bayes Rules! uses it for a Beta-Binomial analysis of the pass rate.

One row per day of the Capital Bikeshare system (registered riders); Bayes Rules! fits rides by stan_glm without grouping, and Section 16.7 treats weekend as a predictor of rides, not a grouping variable.

A simplified version of coffee_ratings (help page): 636 of its batches with farm_name, total_cup_points and nine grades. Bayes Rules! Exercise 17.14 poses a hierarchical model of total cup points by farm on it and leaves the predictors to the reader; filed on coffee_ratings.
One row per U.S. state; region (four levels) classifies the states. Bayes Rules! Chapter 12 fits Normal and Poisson regressions of laws on percent_urban and historical without grouping.
One row per news article; Bayes Rules! Exercise 13.13 models type by logistic regression without grouping.
One row per person; group classifies the 75 people into three arms (control, football players without and with concussion), and nothing repeats within a unit.

A random 1000 hotel bookings, one row each; hotel has two levels, and agent, company and country classify bookings. Bayes Rules! Exercises 13.6-13.9 model is_canceled by logistic regression without grouping.
One species' late-December Ontario counts (loons, 2000-2017), one row per year; the help page points to bird_counts as the more complete table it comes from.
One row per artist of the MoMA collection; country, gender and department classify the artists.
A random sample of 100 artists of the MoMA collection (help page), a subset of moma without department.
One row per penguin (palmerpenguins with above_average_weight added); species and island have three levels each and classify. Bayes Rules! uses it for regression and classification without grouping.
One row per survey respondent; Bayes Rules! Chapter 13 and its exercises fit logistic regressions without grouping.

Two of weather_australia's three stations (help page: weather_australia combines this data with a third city); Bayes Rules! Chapter 11 fits temp3pm by temp9am and location, a two-level fixed predictor.

Daily weather at three stations (Wollongong, Hobart and Uluru), location a design factor of three levels; Bayes Rules! enters location as a fixed predictor (Chapter 11, on the two-station weather_WU).
Daily weather at one station; Bayes Rules! Chapter 13 models raintomorrow by logistic regression without grouping.
One row per level of x, y the successes of n trials; Exam2.B.2 fits glm(y/n ~ x, family = quasibinomial(link = 'probit')) without grouping.
Six rows, two per treatment; Exam2.B.3 fits lm(y ~ trt).
Six rows, obs the row number, Yij the successes of Nij per row; Exam2.B.4 fits glm(Yij/Nij ~ trt, family = quasibinomial(link = 'probit')).
A 2 x 2 factorial, Rep numbering the four replicates of each a x b cell; Exam2.B.7 fits lm(y ~ a + b + a*b) and nested variants without Rep, and four levels make it a design factor at most.
Two treatments, rep the unit of observation (help page: 'unit of observation or observation ID'), one row per unit; Exam3.2 fits glm(F/N ~ trt, family = quasibinomial(link = 'logit')).
X at seven levels with two rows each, F the successes of N; Exam5.1 fits polynomial glm(F/N ~ X + I(X^2) + ..., family = quasibinomial(link = 'logit')) without grouping.
Nine rows of a three-factor main-effects design; Exam5.2 fits sequential lm(y ~ a + b + c).
A two-factor design without a block or unit column; Exam7.1 fits lm(y ~ a + b + a*b) and lm(y ~ a + a %in% b).
An equal-slopes ANCOVA, one row per unit; Exam7.2 fits aov(y ~ trt*x), aov(y ~ trt + x) and aov(y ~ trt).
An unequal-slopes ANCOVA, one row per unit; Exam7.3 fits aov(y ~ trt*x) and lm(y ~ 0 + trt/x).
Example 7.4's A x B factorial with replicate rows per cell and no block or unit column; the package has no example for it.
The response-surface version of Example 7.4, a x b with replicate rows per cell and no block or unit column; the package has no example for it.
One row per x1 x x2 cell; Exam7.6.2.1 fits lm(response ~ x1*x2 + logx1*logx2).
Segmented regression of y on x within a, replicate rows per x and no unit column; Exam7.7 fits lm(y ~ a*bx) on a spline basis bx of x.
One row per level of x, y the successes of Nx trials; Exam1.1 and Exam2.B.1 fit lm and glm(y/Nx ~ x) without grouping.

The author's data-raw/centerexample.R (github.com/flh3/MLMusingR) draws it: set.seed(123), y and x from rnorm for the first cluster, and anscombiser::mimic copies shifted by 2 and 4 for clusters 2 and 3. The help page calls it 60 observations from 3 clusters for discussing within and between group effects.
engage (the complete data) with values deleted for the missing-data example (help page: 'this has missing data'), the same rows and columns.
The help page points to the simulation code of the UCLA OARC page (stats.oarc.ucla.edu/r/codefragments/mesimulation) for its patients nested in doctors nested in hospitals.
A reduced version of thai (help page title 'Thai data from PISA (reduced)', usage data(thai)): 4271 of its rows, with math (thai's pv1math) and six of its columns.
wide: one row per student, the reading scores in fall kindergarten, spring kindergarten and spring first grade as the columns fall_k, spring_k and spring_g1, for growth modeling (help page).
